-- profiles: one row per auth user (id = auth.users.id).
-- Supabase Auth is the identity source — no clerk_id.
create table public.profiles (
  id              uuid primary key references auth.users (id) on delete cascade,
  display_name    text,
  handle          text unique,
  -- style quiz (the prototype's 6 questions)
  archetype       text,            -- Old Money | Smart Casual | Preppy | Streetwear
  palette         text,            -- Neutrals | Earth | Navy | Mono
  fit             text,            -- Tailored | Relaxed | Oversized
  dress_codes     text[],          -- Loungewear | Casual | Smart casual | Business | Black tie
  occasions       text[],          -- Work | Everyday | Weekend | Evening
  nogos           text[],          -- logos | skinny | bright | shorts | ripped | double_denim | graphic | square_toe
  formality_min   int default 1,   -- derived from dress_codes (for the generator's band)
  formality_max   int default 5,
  location_lat    double precision,
  location_lon    double precision,
  locale          text default 'en',
  style_dna       jsonb,
  ootd_streak     int default 0,
  onboarded_at    timestamptz,
  created_at      timestamptz default now()
);

alter table public.profiles enable row level security;

-- A user can read and update only their own profile.
-- (select auth.uid()) is the perf-optimised form; TO authenticated + ownership
-- predicate avoids the BOLA/IDOR trap; update needs both USING and WITH CHECK.
create policy "profiles_select_own"
  on public.profiles for select
  to authenticated
  using ((select auth.uid()) = id);

create policy "profiles_update_own"
  on public.profiles for update
  to authenticated
  using ((select auth.uid()) = id)
  with check ((select auth.uid()) = id);

-- Auto-create the profile row on signup. SECURITY DEFINER so the trigger can
-- insert past RLS; schema-qualified names + empty search_path per Supabase guidance.
create function public.handle_new_user()
returns trigger
language plpgsql
security definer
set search_path = ''
as $$
begin
  insert into public.profiles (id, display_name)
  values (new.id, new.raw_user_meta_data ->> 'full_name');
  return new;
end;
$$;

create trigger on_auth_user_created
  after insert on auth.users
  for each row execute procedure public.handle_new_user();

content.text:
Based on my analysis of the changed files, here's the security assessment:

**Files reviewed in full:**
- `app/generate/actions.ts` — new `saveLocation` server action
- `lib/weather/location.ts` — new `LocationInputSchema` (Zod)
- `components/generate/stylist.tsx` — passes `source: "city"` from client
- `supabase/migrations/20260721090000_authenticated_grants.sql` — DML grants for `authenticated`
- `supabase/migrations/20260721100000_profile_location.sql` — new profile columns
- `lib/generator/types.ts` — adds `timezone` to WeatherPayload
- Both test files (no security surface)

**Traced for concerns:**
- `saveLocation` uses `createClient()` (user-session client, anon key + cookies), calls `getUser()`, and updates with `.eq("id", user.id)`. Zod validates lat/lon ranges, enum source, and bounded label/timezone strings. Backed by the existing `profiles_update_own` RLS policy (`auth.uid() = id` on both USING and WITH CHECK).
- Grants migration: all four current `public` tables (`profiles`, `items`, `outfits`, `outfit_items`, `wear_logs`) have RLS enabled, so blanket table-level DML grant is bounded by RLS. Default privileges apply to future tables, but no such table exists in this diff.
- `d.timezone` is stored but not consumed by any code path in this diff (WeatherPayload.timezone comes from Open-Meteo response, not from the persisted value); no current sink (`Intl.DateTimeFormat`, scheduler, etc.) reads it.
- `d.label` flows to DB → later back to `weather.cityLabel`, rendered as text by React (auto-escaped) — no XSS.
- Lat/lon are numbers per Zod, then interpolated into the Open-Meteo URL via `roundCoord` — no SSRF, no injection.
- Client `source: "city"` label is self-attested but only affects the user's own profile, so no cross-tenant impact.
